'[access] read  page+0x248  from Qt5Gui.dll+0x242c2f',
'[access] read  page+0x360  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x2909b2',
'[access] read  page+0x240  from Qt5Gui.dll+0x23def3',
'[access] read  page+0xa28  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x4546a',
'[access] read  page+0x299  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x454fe      (x8, identical)',
'[access] read  page+0xdf9  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x454fe',
'[access] read  page+0x178  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x45479      (x5, identical)',
'[access] read  page+0x628  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x4546a      (x3, identical)',
'[access] read  page+0x2f9  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x454fe',
'[access] read  page+0xd99  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x454fe',
'[access] read  page+0x248  from Qt5Gui.dll+0x242c2f',
'[access] read  page+0xa8   from ntdll.dll+0x10850',
'[access] read  page+0x240  from Qt5Gui.dll+0x23def3',
'------ and then NOTHING for the next 60 seconds of wall clock ------',
'The whole visible transcript is about 40 [access] lines. There is NO "still watching N page(s)" line',
'anywhere, and NO "=== WRITE into a key field ===" line.',
].join('\n')

const PROCESS_EVIDENCE = [
'Measured at 22:04:25, i.e. about 4 minutes after the probe started:',
'  python.exe    PID 12468  started 22:00:25  cumulative CPU  0.297 s',
'  EVPlayer2.exe PID 6684                    cumulative CPU 487.4 s   (working set 633 MB)',
'  evmedia.exe   PID 27036  started 22:00:29  cumulative CPU   4.3 s   (that is the grab run',
'                                                                      writing verify_out3/)',
'The probe was launched with argument 300, so its own lifetime was 300 seconds.',
'The connection between those figures and the transcript is itself part of what is being judged.',
].join('\n')

const CONTEXT = [
'Repo: D:\\Codes\\github\\ev-reverse  (a reverse-engineering project for EVPlayer2, a Chinese',
'course-video player). Read files with absolute paths.',
'',
'The instrument under diagnosis is tools/parser-tools/probe_write.py. Its docstring is long and is',
'itself a record of measurements made against stand-in target processes. Read it in full before',
'reasoning. Its JavaScript is an inline string inside that Python file.',
'',
'Ticket context: .scratch/offline-keys-and-bench/issues/07-catch-the-key-writing-instruction.md',
'Stand-in harness used for the earlier measurements (temp dir; read if present):',
'  C:\\Users\\Yonjay\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\watchprobe\\drive6.py',
'  C:\\Users\\Yonjay\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\watchprobe\\src\\main.rs',
'',
'The thing that must NOT happen: concluding "the player did not write" when what actually happened',
'is "the instrument reported nothing". This project has already made that error once and the ticket',
'records it at length. Both a positive finding and a named negative are acceptable; a muddle is not.',
'',
'Write your structured report fields in English.',
].join('\n')

const HYPOTHESES_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string' },
          confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'evidence', 'confidence'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['findings'],
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    refuted: { type: 'boolean' },
    why: { type: 'string' },
    correction: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['refuted', 'why'],
}

const LENSES = [
  {
    key: 'js-semantics',
    body: [
      'Read tools/parser-tools/probe_write.py and trace, for the live-player case only:',
      ' - the early return at the top of onAccess and the INDIVIDUAL_CAP gate: after how many reports',
      '   does printing stop, and does that gate do anything else? Does it stop processing, or only stop',
      '   printing?',
      ' - the "still watching" line: under exactly what counter condition does it print, and how many',
      '   seconds of a healthy run separate two of them?',
      ' - the scheduleRearm path: how many MemoryAccessMonitor disable/enable pairs does a run of N',
      '   accesses over M pages perform, and is each pair synchronous with the access that triggered it?',
      ' - the timer callback. What is its first line, what does it do when the found flag is set, and',
      '   which send() is guaranteed to have reached the Python side BEFORE found can be set true?',
      ' - Is there ANY code path that sets found, or clears the interval, without a corresponding',
      '   message the Python side prints?',
      'Report concrete control-flow facts with line numbers.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'frida-cost',
    body: [
      'The script re-arms with setTimeout(...,0) from inside the access callback, and each re-arm does',
      'MemoryAccessMonitor.disable() then .enable() over up to 24 pages. The ticket claims a measurement',
      'that this is free: 100.4% throughput at 64 and 128 pages, 100 ms re-arm, on a stand-in target.',
      'Read C:\\Users\\Yonjay\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\watchprobe\\drive6.py and the Rust source beside it if',
      'present, and say precisely what that stand-in target did: how many pages, how many threads, what',
      'access rate, and which re-arm strategy the free number was measured under. Then state what the',
      'live player looks like by comparison -- see the access lines: Qt5Gui, ntdll and',
      'PlayerLibRender56_vs all touching these pages, in a UPX-packed Qt process with many threads.',
      'Answer directly: is the re-arm-is-free measurement transferable to this run, or was it measured',
      'under conditions that do not hold here? Name the variable that changed.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'output-forensics',
    body: [
      'Establish, with arithmetic where possible:',
      ' - How many [access] lines are in the transcript, and does that number coincide with any constant',
      '   in the script? What does that coincidence imply about how many accesses really occurred?',
      ' - The Python side printed nothing for 60 seconds. Enumerate every reason that could be true: the',
      '   script lost its message channel, the JS thread was starved, the run ended, the terminal panel',
      '   is stale, the process died. For each, say what other evidence in this turn would look',
      '   different if that reason were the true one, and whether that evidence is present or absent.',
      ' - python.exe cumulative CPU is 0.297 s over a ~240 s wall-clock lifetime. What does that number',
      '   rule OUT, and what does it NOT rule out? How much CPU does printing 40 lines and sleeping',
      '   cost? How much would a live frida message channel at even 100 messages/second cost?',
      ' - EVPlayer2.exe shows 487.4 s cumulative CPU. Say plainly whether that can be interpreted at',
      '   all without knowing when the process started, and if not, say so rather than inferring.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'rival-hypotheses',
    body: [
      'Note first that this run DID satisfy the precondition the earlier failed run lacked: 70 contexts',
      'hold a key and the highest decrypted index is 165, so the player was decrypting. Take that',
      'seriously rather than assuming the old negative.',
      'Evaluate these rival explanations on the evidence, and say for each whether it is supported,',
      'refuted, or undecidable:',
      ' (a) The player genuinely did not store into any watched key field during the window, and the only',
      '     defect is that the run went silent before it could report that.',
      ' (b) The found flag became true, the run correctly caught a store, and the report was printed but',
      '     is not in the visible transcript.',
      ' (c) The player was thrown into a near-hang by the guards, so it stopped decrypting -- the',
      '     instrument perturbed the thing it was measuring.',
      ' (d) The watched contexts, index 166..177, are simply not the ones the player writes next, so the',
      '     guards were on the wrong pages entirely.',
      ' (e) The page-guard mechanism is sound and the silence is purely a reporting-path failure.',
      'For each, what would have to be true, and does the transcript show it? A read of page+0x250 was',
      'reported as a WRITE five times -- consider what that says about whether the guard is catching',
      'stores at all, and what it says about whether 0x250 could be a watched key field.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
]

phase('Investigate')
const results = await pipeline(
  LENSES,
  lens => agent(CONTEXT + '\n\n' + TERMINAL + '\n\n' + PROCESS_EVIDENCE + '\n\nYOUR LENS, ' +
    lens.key + ':\n' + lens.body,
    { label: 'probe:' + lens.key, phase: 'Investigate', schema: HYPOTHESES_SCHEMA }),
  (report, lens) => {
    if (!report || !report.findings || !report.findings.length) return null
    const claims = report.findings
      .map(f => '- [' + f.confidence + '] ' + f.claim + ' (evidence: ' + f.evidence + ')')
      .join('\n')
    const vantage = ['correctness', 'does-it-reproduce', 'alternative-cause']
    return parallel(vantage.map(v => () =>
      agent(CONTEXT + '\n\n' + TERMINAL + '\n\n' + PROCESS_EVIDENCE +
        '\n\nAn analyst working the "' + lens.key + '" lens produced these claims about the probe run:\n\n' +
        claims +
        '\n\nYOUR JOB: try to REFUTE them, from the "' + v + '" vantage. Read probe_write.py yourself first.' +
        ' Default to refuted=true when a claim outruns the evidence, when it is stated more confidently than' +
        ' the transcript supports, or when a simpler explanation fits the same facts. Refute in particular' +
        ' any claim that cannot be distinguished from "the instrument reported nothing" -- that' +
        ' indistinguishability is the exact failure this ticket exists to eliminate. Set refuted=false ONLY' +
        ' for claims the evidence positively and unambiguously supports. In the correction field, give the' +
        ' more defensible version of any claim you refute.',
        { label: 'refute:' + lens.key + ':' + v, phase: 'Refute', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA })))
      .then(verdicts => ({ lens: lens.key, claims: report.findings, verdicts: verdicts.filter(Boolean) }))
  },
)

const living = results.filter(Boolean)
const surviving = []
for (const group of living) {
  for (const claim of group.claims) {
    const votes = group.verdicts
    surviving.push({
      lens: group.lens,
      claim: claim.claim,
      confidence: claim.confidence,
      refuted_votes: votes.filter(v => v.refuted).length,
      total_votes: votes.length,
      corrections: votes.filter(v => v.refuted && v.correction).map(v => v.correction),
    })
  }
}

phase('Synthesize')
const SYNTH_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    root_cause: { type: 'string' },
    what_is_certain: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    what_is_not_established: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    fix: { type: 'string' },
    next_command: { type: 'string' },
    ticket_update: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['root_cause', 'what_is_certain', 'what_is_not_established', 'fix', 'next_command', 'ticket_update'],
}

const synthesis = await agent(CONTEXT + '\n\n' + TERMINAL + '\n\n' + PROCESS_EVIDENCE +
  '\n\nFour analysts examined the run from four lenses, and each of their claims was then attacked by' +
  ' three adversarial verifiers. Here is every claim with its refutation tally:\n\n' +
  JSON.stringify(surviving, null, 2) +
  '\n\nWrite the verdict. Requirements:\n' +
  '- root_cause: the single explanation best supported by the evidence. If the evidence cannot decide' +
  ' between "the instrument went deaf" and "the player did not write", say exactly that and say which' +
  ' measurement would decide it.\n' +
  '- what_is_certain: only facts that survived refutation.\n' +
  '- what_is_not_established: name them explicitly. This project has been burned by a conclusion' +
  ' outliving its evidence.\n' +
  '- fix: the concrete change to probe_write.py that removes the ambiguity. Weigh the competing' +
  ' pressures honestly: the re-arm must be fast enough not to miss a store, and cheap enough not to' +
  ' starve the JS thread or throttle the player. Consider rate-limiting the re-arm, reducing the page' +
  ' count, dropping the per-access send after the cap in favour of a periodic heartbeat that proves the' +
  ' run is alive, and making that heartbeat independent of the same mechanism it reports on.\n' +
  '- next_command: the exact command line to run next, using the conda python at' +
  ' C:\\Users\\Yonjay\\.conda\\envs\\subgen\\python.exe, with its preconditions stated.\n' +
  '- ticket_update: a short factual paragraph, in English, to append to ticket 07 recording this run.\n' +
  'Be concrete and terse. No hedging language that hides an absence of evidence.',
  { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', schema: SYNTH_SCHEMA })

return { surviving, synthesis }

'records it at length. Both a positive finding and a named negative are acceptable; a muddle is not.',
'',
'Write your structured report fields in English.',
].join('\n')

const HYPOTHESES_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string' },
          confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
        },
        required: ['claim', 'evidence', 'confidence'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['findings'],
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    refuted: { type: 'boolean' },
    why: { type: 'string' },
    correction: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['refuted', 'why'],
}

const LENSES = [
  {
    key: 'js-semantics',
    body: [
      'Read tools/parser-tools/probe_write.py and trace, for the live-player case only:',
      ' - the early return at the top of onAccess and the INDIVIDUAL_CAP gate: after how many reports',
      '   does printing stop, and does that gate do anything else? Does it stop processing, or only stop',
      '   printing?',
      ' - the "still watching" line: under exactly what counter condition does it print, and how many',
      '   seconds of a healthy run separate two of them?',
      ' - the scheduleRearm path: how many MemoryAccessMonitor disable/enable pairs does a run of N',
      '   accesses over M pages perform, and is each pair synchronous with the access that triggered it?',
      ' - the timer callback. What is its first line, what does it do when the found flag is set, and',
      '   which send() is guaranteed to have reached the Python side BEFORE found can be set true?',
      ' - Is there ANY code path that sets found, or clears the interval, without a corresponding',
      '   message the Python side prints?',
      'Report concrete control-flow facts with line numbers.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'frida-cost',
    body: [
      'The script re-arms with setTimeout(...,0) from inside the access callback, and each re-arm does',
      'MemoryAccessMonitor.disable() then .enable() over up to 24 pages. The ticket claims a measurement',
      'that this is free: 100.4% throughput at 64 and 128 pages, 100 ms re-arm, on a stand-in target.',
      'Read C:\\Users\\Yonjay\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\watchprobe\\drive6.py and the Rust source beside it if',
      'present, and say precisely what that stand-in target did: how many pages, how many threads, what',
      'access rate, and which re-arm strategy the free number was measured under. Then state what the',
      'live player looks like by comparison -- see the access lines: Qt5Gui, ntdll and',
      'PlayerLibRender56_vs all touching these pages, in a UPX-packed Qt process with many threads.',
      'Answer directly: is the re-arm-is-free measurement transferable to this run, or was it measured',
      'under conditions that do not hold here? Name the variable that changed.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'output-forensics',
    body: [
      'Establish, with arithmetic where possible:',
      ' - How many [access] lines are in the transcript, and does that number coincide with any constant',
      '   in the script? What does that coincidence imply about how many accesses really occurred?',
      ' - The Python side printed nothing for 60 seconds. Enumerate every reason that could be true: the',
      '   script lost its message channel, the JS thread was starved, the run ended, the terminal panel',
      '   is stale, the process died. For each, say what other evidence in this turn would look',
      '   different if that reason were the true one, and whether that evidence is present or absent.',
      ' - python.exe cumulative CPU is 0.297 s over a ~240 s wall-clock lifetime. What does that number',
      '   rule OUT, and what does it NOT rule out? How much CPU does printing 40 lines and sleeping',
      '   cost? How much would a live frida message channel at even 100 messages/second cost?',
      ' - EVPlayer2.exe shows 487.4 s cumulative CPU. Say plainly whether that can be interpreted at',
      '   all without knowing when the process started, and if not, say so rather than inferring.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'rival-hypotheses',
    body: [
      'Note first that this run DID satisfy the precondition the earlier failed run lacked: 70 contexts',
      'hold a key and the highest decrypted index is 165, so the player was decrypting. Take that',
      'seriously rather than assuming the old negative.',
      'Evaluate these rival explanations on the evidence, and say for each whether it is supported,',
      'refuted, or undecidable:',
      ' (a) The player genuinely did not store into any watched key field during the window, and the only',
      '     defect is that the run went silent before it could report that.',
      ' (b) The found flag became true, the run correctly caught a store, and the report was printed but',
      '     is not in the visible transcript.',
      ' (c) The player was thrown into a near-hang by the guards, so it stopped decrypting -- the',
      '     instrument perturbed the thing it was measuring.',
      ' (d) The watched contexts, index 166..177, are simply not the ones the player writes next, so the',
      '     guards were on the wrong pages entirely.',
      ' (e) The page-guard mechanism is sound and the silence is purely a reporting-path failure.',
      'For each, what would have to be true, and does the transcript show it? A read of page+0x250 was',
      'reported as a WRITE five times -- consider what that says about whether the guard is catching',
      'stores at all, and what it says about whether 0x250 could be a watched key field.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
]

phase('Investigate')
const results = await pipeline(
  LENSES,
  lens => agent(CONTEXT + '\n\n' + TERMINAL + '\n\n' + PROCESS_EVIDENCE + '\n\nYOUR LENS, ' +
    lens.key + ':\n' + lens.body,
    { label: 'probe:' + lens.key, phase: 'Investigate', schema: HYPOTHESES_SCHEMA }),
  (report, lens) => {
    if (!report || !report.findings || !report.findings.length) return null
    const claims = report.findings
      .map(f => '- [' + f.confidence + '] ' + f.claim + ' (evidence: ' + f.evidence + ')')
      .join('\n')
    const vantage = ['correctness', 'does-it-reproduce', 'alternative-cause']
    return parallel(vantage.map(v => () =>
      agent(CONTEXT + '\n\n' + TERMINAL + '\n\n' + PROCESS_EVIDENCE +
        '\n\nAn analyst working the "' + lens.key + '" lens produced these claims about the probe run:\n\n' +
        claims +
        '\n\nYOUR JOB: try to REFUTE them, from the "' + v + '" vantage. Read probe_write.py yourself first.' +
        ' Default to refuted=true when a claim outruns the evidence, when it is stated more confidently than' +
        ' the transcript supports, or when a simpler explanation fits the same facts. Refute in particular' +
        ' any claim that cannot be distinguished from "the instrument reported nothing" -- that' +
        ' indistinguishability is the exact failure this ticket exists to eliminate. Set refuted=false ONLY' +
        ' for claims the evidence positively and unambiguously supports. In the correction field, give the' +
        ' more defensible version of any claim you refute.',
        { label: 'refute:' + lens.key + ':' + v, phase: 'Refute', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA })))
      .then(verdicts => ({ lens: lens.key, claims: report.findings, verdicts: verdicts.filter(Boolean) }))
  },
)

const living = results.filter(Boolean)
const surviving = []
for (const group of living) {
  for (const claim of group.claims) {
    const votes = group.verdicts
    surviving.push({
      lens: group.lens,
      claim: claim.claim,
      confidence: claim.confidence,
      refuted_votes: votes.filter(v => v.refuted).length,
      total_votes: votes.length,
      corrections: votes.filter(v => v.refuted && v.correction).map(v => v.correction),
    })
  }
}

phase('Synthesize')
const SYNTH_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    root_cause: { type: 'string' },
    what_is_certain: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    what_is_not_established: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    fix: { type: 'string' },
    next_command: { type: 'string' },
    ticket_update: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['root_cause', 'what_is_certain', 'what_is_not_established', 'fix', 'next_command', 'ticket_update'],
}

const synthesis = await agent(CONTEXT + '\n\n' + TERMINAL + '\n\n' + PROCESS_EVIDENCE +
  '\n\nFour analysts examined the run from four lenses, and each of their claims was then attacked by' +
  ' three adversarial verifiers. Here is every claim with its refutation tally:\n\n' +
  JSON.stringify(surviving, null, 2) +
  '\n\nWrite the verdict. Requirements:\n' +
  '- root_cause: the single explanation best supported by the evidence. If the evidence cannot decide' +
  ' between "the instrument went deaf" and "the player did not write", say exactly that and say which' +
  ' measurement would decide it.\n' +
  '- what_is_certain: only facts that survived refutation.\n' +
  '- what_is_not_established: name them explicitly. This project has been burned by a conclusion' +
  ' outliving its evidence.\n' +
  '- fix: the concrete change to probe_write.py that removes the ambiguity. Weigh the competing' +
  ' pressures honestly: the re-arm must be fast enough not to miss a store, and cheap enough not to' +
  ' starve the JS thread or throttle the player. Consider rate-limiting the re-arm, reducing the page' +
  ' count, dropping the per-access send after the cap in favour of a periodic heartbeat that proves the' +
  ' run is alive, and making that heartbeat independent of the same mechanism it reports on.\n' +
  '- next_command: the exact command line to run next, using the conda python at' +
  ' C:\\Users\\Yonjay\\.conda\\envs\\subgen\\python.exe, with its preconditions stated.\n' +
  '- ticket_update: a short factual paragraph, in English, to append to ticket 07 recording this run.\n' +
  'Be concrete and terse. No hedging language that hides an absence of evidence.',
  { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', schema: SYNTH_SCHEMA })

return { surviving, synthesis }

分析在后台跑。现在给用户一个中文回复。

用户的消息是"中文？？？？"——他可能是指我没用中文。我应该：
1. 承认并改用中文
2. 汇报我发现的东西

关键内容（中文）：

**先说结论**：这次 probe_write.py 的运行，在第 40 行 `[access]` 之后就彻底哑了，而它本该每 20 秒打印一行「still watching」。所以这次运行**没有**抓住写指令，而且**不能**据此说「播放器没写密钥」——因为仪器在 40 次访问之后就聋了。

**几条硬事实**：
1. 这次运行**首次满足**工单 07 的前提：611 个 context、70 个有密钥、最高已解密 index=165，瞄准 166..177。播放器真的在解密。
2. 输出正好停在 ~40 行 —— 恰好是脚本里的 `INDIVIDUAL_CAP = 40`。之后只打印"命中"，所以就静默了。
3. 但 `still watching` 每 20 秒一行，**一行都没有**。跑了 4 分钟该有 12 行。→ 说明 JS 侧的 `setInterval` 回调被饿死了，或者定时器被清了。
4. python.exe 累计 CPU **0.297 秒**（4 分钟里）——消息通道几乎是空的。
5. 抓到了 5 次 `write page+0x250 from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x5d39d3`。**这说明 guard 确实能抓到 store**，是机器在动。但 0x250 不在被监视的 key field 范围内（否则会打印 `<<< lands on a key field`），所以不是答案。
6. **两个仪器同时挂在 pid 6684 上**：probe 在页上设 guard，`grab` 在全内存扫描。grab 的扫描读内存 → 读到带 guard 的页 → 触发 probe 的 onAccess → probe 每次访问都 disable+enable 24 个页。这会把 JS 线程和播放器一起拖垮。

抱歉，之前一直没用中文，是我的错。以下是这一轮的结论。

**这次 `probe_write.py` 的运行没有抓住写指令，而且不能据此说「播放器没写密钥」——因为仪器在第 40 次访问之后就聋了。**

几条硬事实：

**第一,这次运行第一次满足工单 07 的前提条件。** `611 个 context、70 个有密钥、最高已解密 index=165、瞄准 166..177`。之前那两次失败运行是「140 个 context、139 个空、最高已解密 index=0」——播放器根本没在解密。这次它在解密。所以这次不是老问题,是新问题。

**第二,输出正好停在约 40 行 `[access]`,而这恰好是脚本里的 `INDIVIDUAL_CAP = 40`。** 超过 40 次之后只打印「命中」,所以日志静默是设计如此,本身不算故障。

**第三,真正的故障是:一行 `still watching` 都没有。** 那行每 20 秒打印一次(脚本第 343 行,`ticks % 20 === 0`)。跑了四分钟,本该有 12 行,一行无。而 python.exe 在四分钟里累计 CPU 只有 **0.297 秒**——消息通道基本是空的。这两条合起来说明:JS 侧那个 `setInterval` 回调被饿死了,或者定时器在第一轮就被清掉了。

**第四,guard 确实能抓到 store。** 日志里有五次 `write page+0x250 from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x5d39d3`。机器是活的。但 `0x250` 不在被监视的 key field 区间内(否则会打 `<<< lands on a key field`),所以这不是答案。

**第五,也是我先前漏看的:两个仪器同时挂在同一个 pid 上。** 终端 2 是 `evmedia.exe grab --pid 6684 --output verify_out3 --mp4`,probe 也是 pid 6684。probe 在被监视的页上设 PAGE_GUARD,`grab` 在全内存反复扫描——而**扫内存就是读内存,读到带 guard 的页就会触发 probe 的回调**,probe 每次回调又对整个 24 页做一次 `disable()` + `enable()`。这很可能就是那场访问风暴的放大器。

我的初步判断是根因在 `setTimeout(...,0)` 那条「每次访问都重装」路径上。工单里把重装记为「免费」(100.4% 吞吐),但那次测量是在**单线程替身、1 个页**上做的;这里是**16 线程的真实 Qt 播放器 + 24 个页 + 另一个进程在狂扫**。变量变了,那个结论不能外推——这正是这个项目反复吃亏的那种「结论活得比证据久」。

我已经派了四路分析加对抗性验证在后台跑(任务 `wna6y05u8`),专门来区分「仪器聋了」和「播放器没写」这两件事,并给出修复方案和下一次的准确命令。结果出来我再报。

两个立刻可用的东西:一是下次别让 probe 和 grab 同时跑同一个 pid;二是修复方向已经清楚——重装必须限速,并且要有一个**不依赖那个定时器本身**的心跳,否则它永远无法报告自己死了。

replaces `if (chooseTargets()) arm();` (which needs PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll and a live player) with a
direct arm over the storm target's pages, and `Process.getModuleByName` is stubbed because a Rust
process has no such module. scheduleRearm, onAccess and arm are untouched.

The two arms of the test:
  REARM_FLOOR_MS = 2   the shipped policy. Expect heartbeats throughout the storm, then a catch.
  REARM_FLOOR_MS = 0   the policy before the fix -- one disable/enable per access. Expect the
                       heartbeat to starve. If it does NOT starve, the fix is unjustified and the
                       claim in the ticket is wrong; that is the falsification this exists for.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import frida

SRC = r"C:\Users\Yonjay\AppData\Local\Temp\watchprobe\src\storm.rs"
EXE = r"C:\Users\Yonjay\AppData\Local\Temp\watchprobe\storm.exe"
PROBE = r"D:\Codes\github\ev-reverse\tools\parser-tools\probe_write.py"


def extract_js():
    text = open(PROBE, encoding="utf-8").read()
    m = re.search(r'JS = r"""(.*?)\n"""', text, re.S)
    if not m:
        print("could not extract the JS out of probe_write.py")
        sys.exit(1)
    return m.group(1)


def build():
    r = subprocess.run(["rustc", "-O", "-o", EXE, SRC],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode:
        print(r.stderr[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def run(floor, secs=22):
    p = subprocess.Popen([EXE], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                         text=True, bufsize=1)
    lines = []
    threading.Thread(target=lambda: [lines.append(l.rstrip()) for l in p.stdout], daemon=True).start()
    for _ in range(400):
        if len(lines) >= 26:
            break
        time.sleep(0.02)
    pid = int([l for l in lines if l.startswith("pid=")][0].split("=")[1])
    pages = [l.split("=")[1] for l in lines if l.startswith("page=")]

    js = extract_js()
    js = js.replace("var dll = Process.getModuleByName(DLL);", "var dll = null;")
    js = js.replace("var REARM_FLOOR_MS = 2;", "var REARM_FLOOR_MS = %d;" % floor)

})();""" % pages_js)
    assert "chooseTargets()) arm()" not in js

    script = session.create_script(js)
    got = []

    t0 = time.monotonic()
    script.load()
    time.sleep(secs)
    try:
        session.detach()
    except Exception:
        pass
    p.kill()

    hbs = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "hb"]
    writes = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "write"]
    # Gap between heartbeats must not exceed ~3x the interval (5 s) for the run to count as reporting.
    stalls = 0
    last = 0.0
    for g in hbs:
        at = g["at"] / 1000.0
        if last and at - last > 15.0:
            stalls += 1
        last = at
    target_writes = len([l for l in lines if l.startswith("write #")])
    print("floor=%-2d  target stores=%-3d  heartbeats=%-3d stalls=%-2d  caught=%-2s  reports=%-6s "
          "rearms=%s" % (

              writes[0]["file"] if writes else "no",
              hbs[-1]["reports"] if hbs else "-",
              hbs[-1]["rearms"] if hbs else "-"))
    return {"heartbeats": len(hbs), "stalls": stalls, "caught": bool(writes),
            "target_writes": target_writes, "reports": hbs[-1]["reports"] if hbs else 0,
            "rearms": hbs[-1]["rearms"] if hbs else 0}


build()

fixed = run(2)
print()
before = run(0)

print("\n--- verdict ---")

print("shipped policy keeps the heartbeat during the storm : %s" % ("YES" if ok_heartbeat else "NO"))
print("shipped policy still catches the store              : %s" % ("YES" if ok_catch else "NO"))

    print("\nFIX VERIFIED: with the fix the run reports; without it, it goes quiet.")
else:
    print("\nNOT VERIFIED -- do not record the fix as working.")

def build():

    if r.returncode:

"""Does the shipped re-arm/ heartbeat policy in probe_write.py survive a many-page storm?

run time, so what runs here is what ships. Only the bootstrap is substituted -- the synthetic driver
replaces `if (chooseTargets()) arm();` (which needs PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll and a live player) with a
direct arm over the storm target's pages, and `Process.getModuleByName` is stubbed because a Rust
process has no such module. scheduleRearm, onAccess and arm are untouched.

Three arms, and the first is the control that keeps the other two honest:
  quiet  floor=2  no storm          proves the heartbeat can fire at all
  storm  floor=2  the shipped policy. Expect heartbeats through the storm, then a catch.
  storm  floor=0  the policy before the fix -- one disable/enable per access. Expect starvation.

If the quiet arm shows no heartbeats, the test is broken and says nothing about the storm. If the
storm arms show the same count as the quiet arm, the fix is unjustified and the ticket claim is wrong.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import frida

SRC = r"C:\Users\Yonjay\AppData\Local\Temp\watchprobe\src\storm.rs"
EXE = r"C:\Users\Yonjay\AppData\Local\Temp\watchprobe\storm.exe"
PROBE = r"D:\Codes\github\ev-reverse\tools\parser-tools\probe_write.py"

# 12 s storm + 8 s quiet gap, then 24 stores at 200 ms each.
SECS = 34
STORM_MS = 12000


def extract_js():
    text = open(PROBE, encoding="utf-8").read()

        sys.exit(1)
    return m.group(1)


def build():
    r = subprocess.run(["rustc", "-O", "-o", EXE, SRC],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

        sys.exit(1)

                         text=True, bufsize=1)

    # Wait for the banner to be COMPLETE, not for a line count. Counting lines is what broke the
    # first version of this harness: the target prints 26 lines, the wait asked for 27, and the loop
    # burned its full 400 * 20 ms = 8 s timeout before attaching -- which put the quiet arm's attach

    return { page: a, fieldOff: 0x120, file: 'x' + i + '.ts', index: i, ctx: a };
  });

  arm();
})();""" % pages_js)
    assert "chooseTargets()) arm()" not in js

    session = frida.attach(pid)
    script = session.create_script(js)
    got = []
    script.on("message", lambda m, d: got.append(m.get("payload") or {}))
    script.load()
    time.sleep(secs)
    try:
        session.detach()
    except Exception:
        pass
    p.kill()

    kinds = {}

        kinds[g.get("t")] = kinds.get(g.get("t"), 0) + 1
    hbs = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "hb"]
    writes = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "write"]
    stalls = 0
    last = 0.0
    for g in hbs:
        at = g["at"] / 1000.0
        if last and at - last > 15.0:
            stalls += 1
        last = at
    target_writes = len([l for l in lines if l.startswith("write #")])
    print("%-6s floor=%-2d  target stores=%-3d  heartbeats=%-3d stalls=%-2d  caught=%-8s "
          "messages=%s" % (
              label, floor, target_writes, len(hbs), stalls,
              writes[0]["file"] if writes else "no", kinds))

            "target_writes": target_writes}

"""Does the shipped re-arm/ heartbeat policy in probe_write.py survive a many-page storm?

The tested code is not a copy: the JavaScript is EXTRACTED from tools/parser-tools/probe_write.py at
run time, so what runs here is what ships. Only the bootstrap is substituted -- the synthetic driver
replaces `if (chooseTargets()) arm();` (which needs PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll and a live player) with a
direct arm over the storm target's pages, and `Process.getModuleByName` is stubbed because a Rust
process has no such module. scheduleRearm, onAccess and arm are untouched.

Three arms, and the first is the control that keeps the other two honest:
  quiet  floor=2  no storm          proves the heartbeat can fire at all
  storm  floor=2  the shipped policy. Expect heartbeats through the storm, then a catch.
  storm  floor=0  the policy before the fix -- one disable/enable per access. Expect starvation.

If the quiet arm shows no heartbeats, the test is broken and says nothing about the storm. If the
storm arms show the same count as the quiet arm, the fix is unjustified and the ticket claim is wrong.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time

import frida

SRC = r"C:\Users\Yonjay\AppData\Local\Temp\watchprobe\src\storm.rs"
EXE = r"C:\Users\Yonjay\AppData\Local\Temp\watchprobe\storm.exe"
PROBE = r"D:\Codes\github\ev-reverse\tools\parser-tools\probe_write.py"

# 12 s storm + 8 s quiet gap, then 24 stores at 200 ms each.
SECS = 34
STORM_MS = 12000


def extract_js():
    text = open(PROBE, encoding="utf-8").read()
    m = re.search(r'JS = r"""(.*?)\n"""', text, re.S)
    if not m:
        print("could not extract the JS out of probe_write.py")
        sys.exit(1)
    return m.group(1)


def build():
    r = subprocess.run(["rustc", "-O", "-o", EXE, SRC],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode:
        print(r.stderr[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def run(label, floor, storm_ms, secs=SECS, pages_n=24):
    p = subprocess.Popen([EXE, str(storm_ms)], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                         text=True, bufsize=1)
    lines = []
    threading.Thread(target=lambda: [lines.append(l.rstrip()) for l in p.stdout], daemon=True).start()
    # Wait for the banner to be COMPLETE, not for a line count. Counting lines is what broke the
    # first version of this harness: the target prints 26 lines, the wait asked for 27, and the loop
    # burned its full 400 * 20 ms = 8 s timeout before attaching -- which put the quiet arm's attach
    # right at the moment its stores begin and made a working heartbeat look starved.
    for _ in range(400):
        if any(l.startswith("storm_ms=") for l in lines):
            break
        time.sleep(0.02)
    assert any(l.startswith("storm_ms=") for l in lines), "the target never finished its banner"
    pid = int([l for l in lines if l.startswith("pid=")][0].split("=")[1])
    pages = [l.split("=")[1] for l in lines if l.startswith("page=")]

    js = extract_js()
    js = js.replace("var dll = Process.getModuleByName(DLL);", "var dll = null;")
    js = js.replace("var REARM_FLOOR_MS = 2;", "var REARM_FLOOR_MS = %d;" % floor)
    assert "var REARM_FLOOR_MS = %d;" % floor in js, "the floor constant moved -- update this test"
    pages_js = ", ".join("'0x" + a + "'" for a in pages[:pages_n])
    js = js.replace("if (chooseTargets()) arm();", """(function () {
  var PAGES = [%s];
  watched = PAGES.map(function (a, i) {
    return { page: a, fieldOff: 0x120, file: 'x' + i + '.ts', index: i, ctx: a };
  });
  ranges = PAGES.map(function (a) { return { base: ptr(a), size: 0x1000 }; });
  focus = watched[0];
  arm();
})();""" % pages_js)
    assert "chooseTargets()) arm()" not in js

    session = frida.attach(pid)
    script = session.create_script(js)
    got = []
    script.on("message", lambda m, d: got.append(m.get("payload") or {}))
    script.load()
    time.sleep(secs)
    try:
        session.detach()
    except Exception:
        pass
    p.kill()

    kinds = {}
    for g in got:
        kinds[g.get("t")] = kinds.get(g.get("t"), 0) + 1
    hbs = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "hb"]
    writes = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "write"]
    stalls = 0
    last = 0.0
    for g in hbs:
        at = g["at"] / 1000.0
        if last and at - last > 15.0:
            stalls += 1
        last = at
    target_writes = len([l for l in lines if l.startswith("write #")])
    print("%-6s floor=%-2d pages=%-2d  target stores=%-3d  heartbeats=%-3d stalls=%-2d  caught=%-8s "
          "messages=%s" % (
              label, floor, len(pages[:pages_n]), target_writes, len(hbs), stalls,
              writes[0]["file"] if writes else "no", kinds))
    return {"heartbeats": len(hbs), "stalls": stalls, "caught": bool(writes),
            "target_writes": target_writes}

## Run 3: the precondition was met for the first time, and the instrument went dark

The run of 2026-09-13 is the first one that was not the benign "already decrypted" case:

```
[*] found 611 context(s), 541 with an empty key field
[*] 70 of 611 context(s) hold a key; the highest decrypted index is 165
[*] aiming at 24 context(s), index 166..177
[*] guards armed. 请保持播放。
[access] read  page+0x240  from Qt5Gui.dll+0x23def3
... about 40 access lines, five of them:
[access] write page+0x250  from PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll+0x5d39d3
... and then nothing at all for the remaining minutes.
```

What that does establish: `0x5d39d3` really is storing into a watched page and the guard really does
catch stores, so the mechanism is sound. `page+0x250` is not a watched key field, so those five are
not the answer.

What it does **not** establish: anything about whether the player wrote a key. The line count is
exactly `INDIVIDUAL_CAP`, and the heartbeat is emitted every 20 ticks of a 1000 ms timer independently
of the cap and independently of any write — so a player that merely abstained could not have
suppressed it. **The silence is instrument-side.** The run is VOID, not a negative.

A second instrument was attached to the same pid throughout: `evmedia grab --pid 6684`. It reads
`ctx+0x120` itself on every poll (`crates/evmedia-win/src/scan.rs`, `active_keys` reads the whole
0x2a8-byte object; `OFF_SCHEDULE` is 0x120), so it was reading the exact field under guard, and its
`regions()` walk (`crates/evmedia-win/src/process.rs`) skips pages that show `PAGE_GUARD` at the
moment it enumerates and is re-enumerated per poll. It cannot explain the missing heartbeat, which is
independent of the pages — but it is an unexcluded confounder and the two instruments must not share
a pid again.

read in tight loops by four threads, then 24 stores at `page+0x120`

unmodified so the thing tested is the thing that ships).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24 | 1 | no | no |
| 8 | 1 | no | no |
| 4 | 1 | no | no |
| 2 | 4 | yes | yes |
| 1 | 4 | yes | yes |
| 2, re-arm floor removed | 1 | no | no |

The ticket's earlier "re-arm is free, 100.4% throughput at 128 pages" measurement was taken on one
page of a single-threaded target that slept between stores. On many hot pages the binding constraint
is not the re-arm churn but the sheer volume of access callbacks, and it takes the instrument — and
the target — down. Four pages is already too many. `MAX_PAGES` is now 2, the re-arm is rate-limited,
and the last row is the mutation: with the floor removed, two pages fail as well.

The storm is harsher than the player, so 2 is a floor on the constraint, not a measurement of the
player. It also means the aiming strategy needs rethinking: watching the 24 contexts of the frontier
was never watchable, so the choice is a smaller, better-chosen window — or the `0x20EC0` hook below,
which costs one hook instead of N guarded pages and is now the more promising of the two.

  target, so the flood was removed rather than the heartbeat explained away.

  shares an event loop with the access callbacks and can be starved by them. Nothing from the agent
  for 18 s prints a VOID warning; the run ends with a message count and says outright that a silent
  run is not a negative about the player.
- `script.on('destroyed')` and `session.on('detached')` both print VOID.
- The script's docstring now states that the grab must not share the pid.

**Still not run against the player.** The next run is the one that answers this ticket, and it must
have the player to itself.

## Second run: the gap was detected and aimed at, and the seek could not be delivered

`verify_out3/`, `target\release\evmedia.exe grab --pid 6684 --output verify_out3 --mp4`, 20 minutes.
This run started with the lesson playing, so it is the first one with a key window, and it answers the
question the artifacts alone could not:

```
  keys=70    urls=71    segments=70    done=54    failed=1    new=70 unreachable=1 elapsed=386s
  caught up with the player; keep playing to reveal more segments
  keys=71    urls=45    segments=70    done=54    failed=1    new=0  unreachable=0 elapsed=429s
  ...
  stalled 5 poll(s) with a gap behind the playhead; sweeping back to index 166
  player is holding no segment window; nothing to aim at
  sweep unavailable; waiting for manual playback instead
  ...
  no progress for 60 polls; stopping
  merged 54 segment(s) -> verify_out3\lesson.partial.ts  [INCOMPLETE]
  refusing to remux an incomplete merge; play the rest and rerun (segments are cached)
```

Against the acceptance criteria:

- **A lesson is open and the playhead jumped forward leaving a gap.** Yes — `a gap behind the
  playhead` is the sweep's own words.
- **The sweep reports detecting the gap and aiming a seek at it.** Yes, and this is the criterion the
  first run could not answer: `sweeping back to index 166` is the detection *and* the aim.
- **The merge is complete, with no index missing.** No. 54 segments merged, `[INCOMPLETE]`, and
  `--mp4` correctly refused to remux a partial merge rather than write a broken file.
- **The command and its output are recorded.** Yes, above.

So gap detection and aiming work against a real gap. The failure is one step later and is now named:
**`player is holding no segment window; nothing to aim at`** — the sweep computed the target index
correctly and then had nothing to seek, because the player had released its segment window by the
time the sweep ran. That is the next thing to look at, and it is a different defect from the one this
ticket was opened for.

Two smaller facts worth carrying: `done=54` means the key path is working end to end — 54 segments
decrypted and merged, where the first run decrypted none. And `failed=1` persisted across the whole
run with no reason printed, because the default human reporter discards segment-failure events; the
next run should pass `--json-events` so the failure is on the record.

fix: the write watch could not watch, and the page count was the reason

Run 3 armed on the frontier for the first time (611 contexts, 70 keyed, highest
decrypted index 165) and then went silent after exactly INDIVIDUAL_CAP lines with
its heartbeat never firing once. The heartbeat is emitted on a 1000 ms timer,
independently of the cap and of any write, so a player that merely abstained could
not have suppressed it: the silence is instrument-side, and the run is void rather
than a negative about the player.

The cause turned out not to be the re-arm churn that the earlier one-page,
single-threaded measurement had cleared. Measured against a storm stand-in (24
pages read in tight loops by four threads, then 24 stores at page+0x120, driven by
a harness that extracts this file's own JS so the thing tested is the thing that
ships): at 24, 8 and 4 guarded pages the target does not even finish its own storm
and no store is caught; at 2 and at 1 the run keeps its heartbeat and catches the
store. MAX_PAGES is 2 for that reason. The rate limit is also load-bearing --
removing REARM_FLOOR_MS at two pages reproduces the failure exactly.

The rest is about not being able to tell "the instrument went deaf" from "the
player did not write":
- the heartbeat fires at arm time as well as every 5 s, and carries reports,
  rearms and pages, which were previously unreported
- liveness is judged Python-side on ANY message, because the heartbeat shares an
  event loop with the access callbacks and can be starved by them
- destroyed/detached print VOID, and a silent run ends by saying outright that it
  is not a negative about the player
- the focus page prints its writes uncapped; printing all its accesses was tried
  and is itself a flood, which held the heartbeat to a single beat
- the docstring says the grab must not share a pid, and why

Ticket 07 records the run, the measurement table, and the fact that this still has
not run against the player.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
fix: the write watch never re-armed, and three claims about the DLL were wrong

probe_write.py armed a page guard twice and caught nothing in two 240-second runs. The mechanism was
tested against stand-in targets written for the purpose, and the cause is not "the player never wrote":

* a PAGE_GUARD is consumed by the FIRST access, read or write, and frida does not restore it.
  Measured: 27 target memory operations, 1 report. The player reads these context objects constantly,
  so the first read silenced the watch for the rest of the run and nothing was reported.
* re-arming from inside the access callback WEDGES the target. Measured: 200 reports and the target
  performed zero operations for 8 seconds.
* re-arming from a timer is free: 100.4% of unguarded throughput at 64 and 128 pages.
* the reported address is the faulting byte, not the write's first byte -- a 32-byte store at
  page+0x120 reported as page+0x130, so an exact-field filter throws the answer away.
* a guard faults BEFORE the store runs, so the value has to be read on a later turn.
* NativePointer has no toNumber(); the first version called it on `.and()` inside the callback, which
  raised once per access while looking perfectly armed.
* Thread exposes only `backtrace` on this build: no hardware watchpoints exist on frida 17.18.0, so the
  ticket's own fallback, a per-thread breakpoint, was never available.

The rewrite aims at the contexts just past the highest decrypted index instead of an arbitrary one,
guards up to 24 pages, re-arms on a 100 ms timer and never from inside the callback, reports every
access, reads the value after the store has completed, and falls back to scanning the stack for module
pointers when the unwind-based backtrace comes back empty. Verified end to end against a stand-in:
six reads of the guarded page, then a 32-byte store -- it survived the reads, caught the store, named
the instruction, dumped the registers, read the value back correctly, and produced a call chain after
both backtracers returned nothing.

This also corrects what the bench believed about watch_key.py: 128 guarded pages measured free, so the
hang is not the page count. It is the AES-site hook taking an ACCURATE backtrace on every AES round.

Disassembling the DLL from the file then showed three claims in the tickets were wrong:

* 0x792c78 is `xor ebp,[rsi-8]`, a round-key XOR, not an inverse-S-box read. Its enclosing function is
  [0x792b1c, 0x792ec3).
* ticket 06's recipe for finding a function entry -- scan back for `cc cc cc` -- is wrong: there is no
  cc run anywhere in [0x792000, 0x792c78), and the nearest one is AES_set_encrypt_key's entry, so the
  recipe returns a different function. `.pdata` gives the answer exactly, and this DLL has it: 19,488
  entries.
* ticket 03 deleted aes_map.py and aes_disasm.py because "this machine has no disassembler". capstone
  5.0.7 and pefile 2024.8.26 are both installed in the conda env. That note was most likely written
  against the PATH `python`, which is a Microsoft Store placeholder and has neither.

And it located the AES oracle ticket 06 needs: the app's key setup at 0x20EC0 (mode selects encrypt or
decrypt and stores the block function at ctx+0x118), its block-call trampoline at 0x20EA0, and the
two -- and only two -- places in the whole .text that use `add rcx,0x120`, which are the segment-key
field's consumers, both of them passing that field to this AES.

45 tests pass; nothing in Rust changed.

| `scan_keys_all.py` | `harvest_keys.py` with a better target set; superseded the same way. |

| `ev2_grab.py` | The entire Python pipeline, harvest through merge; the Rust `grab` does all of it, including resume. |
| `drive_playhead.py` | Posts arrow keys to steer the playhead; `evmedia-win::playhead` does this, and its docstring says so. |

| `compare_tk.py` | Exists only to feed the tk-derivation family, which is the same disproven formula. |
| `find_b64.py` | Locates the base64 decoder by watching alphabet tables; repeated full-memory runs found nothing, and ticket 06 no longer needs the decoder. |
| `aes_map.py` | Static function-boundary mapping of the AES region. **Deleted on a false premise — see the correction below.** |
| `aes_disasm.py` | Same static route to the same RVA. **Deleted on a false premise — see the correction below.** |

| `find_segments.ps1` | Its RVAs point at this build's M3U8 parser, not at key derivation. It has failed every time it was run. |

"""How many hot pages can probe_write.py actually watch?

The tested code is not a copy: the JavaScript is EXTRACTED from
tools/parser-tools/probe_write.py at run time, so what runs here is what ships. Only the bootstrap is
substituted -- the synthetic driver replaces `if (chooseTargets()) arm();`, which needs
PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll and a live player, with a direct arm over the storm target's pages.
scheduleRearm, onAccess, beat and arm are untouched. `Process.getModuleByName` is stubbed because a
Rust process has none.

Arms:
  quiet   floor=2, no storm            control. If this shows no heartbeat, the harness is broken and
                                       nothing the storm arms say means anything.
  storm   floor=2, sweep of page counts
  mutant  floor=2 -> 0 at the largest workable count. This is the falsification: if the unthrottled
                                       re-arm does just as well, the rate limit is not load-bearing
                                       and the ticket's claim about it is wrong.

Usage:  <python> -u storm_test.py [page counts...]
        defaults to 24 8 4 2 1

The built target goes to the OS temp directory; nothing is written into the repo.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

import frida

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SRC = HERE / "storm.rs"
EXE = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "ev-storm" / "storm.exe"
PROBE = HERE.parent / "probe_write.py"

# 12 s storm + 8 s quiet gap, then 24 stores at 200 ms each.
SECS = 34
STORM_MS = 12000


def extract_js():
    text = PROBE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r'JS = r"""(.*?)\n"""', text, re.S)
    if not m:
        print("could not extract the JS out of %s" % PROBE)
        sys.exit(1)
    return m.group(1)


def build():
    EXE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    r = subprocess.run(["rustc", "-O", "-o", str(EXE), str(SRC)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode:
        print(r.stderr[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def run(label, floor, storm_ms, secs=SECS, pages_n=24):
    p = subprocess.Popen([str(EXE), str(storm_ms)], stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                         stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, bufsize=1)
    lines = []
    threading.Thread(target=lambda: [l for l in p.stdout and lines.append(l.rstrip())],
                     daemon=True).start()
    # Wait for the banner to be COMPLETE, not for a line count. Counting lines is what broke the
    # first version of this harness: the target prints 26 lines, the wait asked for 27, and the loop
    # burned its full 400 * 20 ms = 8 s timeout before attaching -- which put the quiet arm's attach
    # right at the moment its stores begin and made a working heartbeat look starved.
    for _ in range(400):
        if any(l.startswith("storm_ms=") for l in lines):
            break
        time.sleep(0.02)
    assert any(l.startswith("storm_ms=") for l in lines), "the target never finished its banner"
    pid = int([l for l in lines if l.startswith("pid=")][0].split("=")[1])
    pages = [l.split("=")[1] for l in lines if l.startswith("page=")]

    js = extract_js()
    js = js.replace("var dll = Process.getModuleByName(DLL);", "var dll = null;")
    js = js.replace("var REARM_FLOOR_MS = 2;", "var REARM_FLOOR_MS = %d;" % floor)
    assert "var REARM_FLOOR_MS = %d;" % floor in js, "the floor constant moved -- update this test"
    pages_js = ", ".join("'0x" + a + "'" for a in pages[:pages_n])
    js = js.replace("if (chooseTargets()) arm();", """(function () {
  var PAGES = [%s];
  watched = PAGES.map(function (a, i) {
    return { page: a, fieldOff: 0x120, file: 'x' + i + '.ts', index: i, ctx: a };
  });
  ranges = PAGES.map(function (a) { return { base: ptr(a), size: 0x1000 }; });
  focus = watched[0];
  arm();
})();""" % pages_js)
    assert "chooseTargets()) arm()" not in js

    session = frida.attach(pid)
    script = session.create_script(js)
    got = []
    script.on("message", lambda m, d: got.append(m.get("payload") or {}))
    script.load()
    time.sleep(secs)
    try:
        session.detach()
    except Exception:
        pass
    p.kill()

    kinds = {}
    for g in got:
        kinds[g.get("t")] = kinds.get(g.get("t"), 0) + 1
    hbs = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "hb"]
    writes = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "write"]
    stalls = 0
    last = 0.0
    for g in hbs:
        at = g["at"] / 1000.0
        if last and at - last > 15.0:
            stalls += 1
        last = at
    target_writes = len([l for l in lines if l.startswith("write #")])
    print("%-6s floor=%-2d pages=%-2d  target stores=%-3d  heartbeats=%-3d stalls=%-2d  "
          "caught=%-8s messages=%s" % (
              label, floor, len(pages[:pages_n]), target_writes, len(hbs), stalls,
              writes[0]["file"] if writes else "no", kinds))
    return {"heartbeats": len(hbs), "stalls": stalls, "caught": bool(writes),
            "target_writes": target_writes}


def attempt(label, floor, storm_ms, secs=SECS, pages_n=24):
    """An arm that kills the target, or the agent, is a result -- not a crash to hide."""
    try:
        return run(label, floor, storm_ms, secs, pages_n)
    except Exception as e:
        print("%-6s floor=%-2d  ARM DIED: %s: %s" % (label, floor, type(e).__name__, e))
        return {"heartbeats": 0, "stalls": 0, "caught": False, "target_writes": 0, "died": True}


def main():
    counts = [int(a) for a in sys.argv[1:]] or [24, 8, 4, 2, 1]
    build()
    print("target: 24 pages read in tight loops by 4 threads for 12 s, then a quiet gap, "
          "then 24 stores\n")

    attempt("quiet", 2, 0, secs=20)
    print()
    sweep = [(n, attempt("storm", 2, STORM_MS, pages_n=n)) for n in counts]

    print("\n--- how many hot pages this instrument can actually watch ---")
    ok = [n for n, r in sweep if r["heartbeats"] >= 3 and r["caught"] and not r.get("died")]
    print("page counts that stayed live AND caught the store: %s" % (ok or "none"))
    if not ok:
        print("NOTHING WORKS -- the instrument cannot watch even one hot page under this storm.")
        print("Do not record the fix as working.")
        return 1
    best = max(ok)
    print("largest workable page count: %d" % best)
    print("\nmutation: the same run with the re-arm floor removed, at %d page(s)" % best)
    before = attempt("mutant", 0, STORM_MS, pages_n=best)
    worse = before.get("died") or before["heartbeats"] < 3 or not before["caught"]
    print("\nold policy (floor=0) is measurably worse than the floor: %s%s"
          % ("YES" if worse else "NO -- the floor is not what makes this work",
             "  (arm died / target wedged)" if before.get("died") else ""))
    if worse:
        print("\nVERIFIED at %d page(s): throttled it reports and catches; unthrottled it does not."
              % best)
        return 0
    print("\nMUTATION DID NOT BITE -- the rate limit is not load-bearing here; say so.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""How many hot pages can probe_write.py actually watch?

The tested code is not a copy: the JavaScript is EXTRACTED from
tools/parser-tools/probe_write.py at run time, so what runs here is what ships. Only the bootstrap is
substituted -- the synthetic driver replaces `if (chooseTargets()) arm();`, which needs
PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll and a live player, with a direct arm over the storm target's pages.
scheduleRearm, onAccess, beat and arm are untouched. `Process.getModuleByName` is stubbed because a
Rust process has none.

Arms:
  quiet   floor=2, no storm            control. If this shows no heartbeat, the harness is broken and
                                       nothing the storm arms say means anything.
  storm   floor=2, sweep of page counts
  mutant  floor=2 -> 0 at the largest workable count. This is the falsification: if the unthrottled
                                       re-arm does just as well, the rate limit is not load-bearing
                                       and the ticket's claim about it is wrong.

Usage:  <python> -u storm_test.py [page counts...]
        defaults to 24 8 4 2 1

The built target goes to the OS temp directory; nothing is written into the repo.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

import frida

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SRC = HERE / "storm.rs"
EXE = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "ev-storm" / "storm.exe"
PROBE = HERE.parent / "probe_write.py"

# 12 s storm + 8 s quiet gap, then 24 stores at 200 ms each.
SECS = 34
STORM_MS = 12000


def extract_js():
    text = PROBE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    m = re.search(r'JS = r"""(.*?)\n"""', text, re.S)
    if not m:
        print("could not extract the JS out of %s" % PROBE)
        sys.exit(1)
    return m.group(1)


def build():
    EXE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    r = subprocess.run(["rustc", "-O", "-o", str(EXE), str(SRC)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode:
        print(r.stderr[-2000:])
        sys.exit(1)


def run(label, floor, storm_ms, secs=SECS, pages_n=24):
    p = subprocess.Popen([str(EXE), str(storm_ms)], stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                         stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, bufsize=1)
    lines = []
    threading.Thread(target=lambda: [l for l in p.stdout and lines.append(l.rstrip())],
                     daemon=True).start()
    # Wait for the banner to be COMPLETE, not for a line count. Counting lines is what broke the
    # first version of this harness: the target prints 26 lines, the wait asked for 27, and the loop
    # burned its full 400 * 20 ms = 8 s timeout before attaching -- which put the quiet arm's attach
    # right at the moment its stores begin and made a working heartbeat look starved.
    for _ in range(400):
        if any(l.startswith("storm_ms=") for l in lines):
            break
        time.sleep(0.02)
    assert any(l.startswith("storm_ms=") for l in lines), "the target never finished its banner"
    pid = int([l for l in lines if l.startswith("pid=")][0].split("=")[1])
    pages = [l.split("=")[1] for l in lines if l.startswith("page=")]

    js = extract_js()
    js = js.replace("var dll = Process.getModuleByName(DLL);", "var dll = null;")
    js = js.replace("var REARM_FLOOR_MS = 2;", "var REARM_FLOOR_MS = %d;" % floor)
    assert "var REARM_FLOOR_MS = %d;" % floor in js, "the floor constant moved -- update this test"
    pages_js = ", ".join("'0x" + a + "'" for a in pages[:pages_n])
    js = js.replace("if (chooseTargets()) arm();", """(function () {
  var PAGES = [%s];
  watched = PAGES.map(function (a, i) {
    return { page: a, fieldOff: 0x120, file: 'x' + i + '.ts', index: i, ctx: a };
  });
  ranges = PAGES.map(function (a) { return { base: ptr(a), size: 0x1000 }; });
  focus = watched[0];
  arm();
})();""" % pages_js)
    assert "chooseTargets()) arm()" not in js

    session = frida.attach(pid)
    script = session.create_script(js)
    got = []
    script.on("message", lambda m, d: got.append(m.get("payload") or {}))
    script.load()
    time.sleep(secs)
    try:
        session.detach()
    except Exception:
        pass
    p.kill()

    kinds = {}
    for g in got:
        kinds[g.get("t")] = kinds.get(g.get("t"), 0) + 1
    hbs = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "hb"]
    writes = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "write"]
    stalls = 0
    last = 0.0
    for g in hbs:
        at = g["at"] / 1000.0
        if last and at - last > 15.0:
            stalls += 1
        last = at
    target_writes = len([l for l in lines if l.startswith("write #")])
    print("%-6s floor=%-2d pages=%-2d  target stores=%-3d  heartbeats=%-3d stalls=%-2d  "
          "caught=%-8s messages=%s" % (
              label, floor, len(pages[:pages_n]), target_writes, len(hbs), stalls,
              writes[0]["file"] if writes else "no", kinds))
    return {"heartbeats": len(hbs), "stalls": stalls, "caught": bool(writes),
            "target_writes": target_writes}


def attempt(label, floor, storm_ms, secs=SECS, pages_n=24):
    """An arm that kills the target, or the agent, is a result -- not a crash to hide."""
    try:
        return run(label, floor, storm_ms, secs, pages_n)
    except Exception as e:
        print("%-6s floor=%-2d  ARM DIED: %s: %s" % (label, floor, type(e).__name__, e))
        return {"heartbeats": 0, "stalls": 0, "caught": False, "target_writes": 0, "died": True}


def main():
    counts = [int(a) for a in sys.argv[1:]] or [24, 8, 4, 2, 1]
    build()
    print("target: 24 pages read in tight loops by 4 threads for 12 s, then a quiet gap, "
          "then 24 stores\n")

    attempt("quiet", 2, 0, secs=20)
    print()
    sweep = [(n, attempt("storm", 2, STORM_MS, pages_n=n)) for n in counts]

    print("\n--- how many hot pages this instrument can actually watch ---")
    ok = [n for n, r in sweep if r["heartbeats"] >= 3 and r["caught"] and not r.get("died")]
    print("page counts that stayed live AND caught the store: %s" % (ok or "none"))
    if not ok:
        print("NOTHING WORKS -- the instrument cannot watch even one hot page under this storm.")
        print("Do not record the fix as working.")
        return 1
    best = max(ok)
    print("largest workable page count: %d" % best)
    print("\nmutation: the same run with the re-arm floor removed, at %d page(s)" % best)
    before = attempt("mutant", 0, STORM_MS, pages_n=best)
    worse = before.get("died") or before["heartbeats"] < 3 or not before["caught"]
    print("\nold policy (floor=0) is measurably worse than the floor: %s%s"
          % ("YES" if worse else "NO -- the floor is not what makes this work",
             "  (arm died / target wedged)" if before.get("died") else ""))
    if worse:
        print("\nVERIFIED at %d page(s): throttled it reports and catches; unthrottled it does not."
              % best)
        return 0
    print("\nMUTATION DID NOT BITE -- the rate limit is not load-bearing here; say so.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Does setInterval actually fire against an idle Rust target in this frida build?

This exists because a harness bug made the heartbeat look starved. storm_test.py's quiet arm showed
the arm-time beat and then nothing for eight seconds while its storm arm showed several, which is the
signature of either a real defect in probe_write.py's heartbeat or an artefact of the harness -- and
the difference decides whether the heartbeat can be trusted at all.

It was the harness (see storm_test.py). This keeps the narrow question answerable without the storm
attached: one setInterval, one target, no guards, and a count at the end.

Usage:  <python> -u interval_test.py
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

import frida

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SRC = HERE / "storm.rs"
EXE = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "ev-storm" / "storm.exe"

JS = r"""
'use strict';
var n = 0;
setInterval(function () { n++; send({ t: 'tick', n: n, at: Date.now() }); }, 1000);
send({ t: 'armed' });
"""


def main():
    EXE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    r = subprocess.run(["rustc", "-O", "-o", str(EXE), str(SRC)],
                       capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    if r.returncode:
        print(r.stderr[-2000:])
        return 1

    p = subprocess.Popen([str(EXE), "0"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                         text=True, bufsize=1)
    lines = []
    threading.Thread(target=lambda: [lines.append(l.rstrip()) for l in p.stdout],
                     daemon=True).start()
    for _ in range(400):
        if lines:
            break
        time.sleep(0.02)
    pid = int(lines[0].split("=")[1])

    session = frida.attach(pid)
    script = session.create_script(JS)
    got = []
    script.on("message", lambda m, d: got.append(m.get("payload") or {}))
    script.load()
    time.sleep(7)
    try:
        session.detach()
    except Exception:
        pass
    p.kill()

    ticks = [g for g in got if g.get("t") == "tick"]
    print("messages: %s" % got)
    print("a 1s interval over 7s produced %d tick(s)" % len(ticks))
    ok = len(ticks) >= 5
    print("RESULT: %s" % ("setInterval works" if ok else "setInterval DOES NOT FIRE here"))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# 03 — Classify the research bench and delete what the product already covers

**What to build:** Every script under the research bench gets exactly one verdict — the Rust product already covers it, it is still an instrument, or it cannot work against this build — and the covered and dead ones are deleted rather than described. Instruments are left alone: they are the apparatus tickets 06–10 run on, and rewriting them mid-experiment is the thing to avoid.

**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] Every script has a recorded verdict with a one-line reason.
- [x] Scripts whose capability the Rust product already implements are deleted.
- [x] Scripts that cannot work against this build are deleted.
- [x] Instruments survive untouched, and the list of them is what tickets 06–10 draw from.
- [x] Nothing the product or the remaining experiments depend on is deleted.

## Verdicts

31 Python scripts and one PowerShell script, each with one verdict. Twenty-one files were deleted in
all: eighteen Python scripts, the PowerShell script, and two `.cmd` wrappers. Thirteen Python scripts
survive as instruments.

### Covered by the product — deleted

The capability is now implemented in Rust, and the Rust version is the one that is correct. Every
harvest-family script here tests candidates against segment bytes; the bench's versions all predate
the 752-byte probe alignment fix, so their "0 hits" readings were artefacts of the bug.

| Script | Why it goes |
| --- | --- |
| `scan_ctypes.py` | ReadProcessMemory-only key scan — its own docstring names `evmedia-win/scan.rs` as the target, and that is now what the product does. |
| `fast_scan.py` | Scans memory for 32-hex candidates and tests them against the recently-written segments; that candidate path is `keyscan::recover`. |
| `harvest_all.py` | Memory scan, test against every downloaded segment, write JSON — the same job as `grab` plus `keyscan::recover`. |
| `harvest_keys.py` | Collects every 32-hex string and tries each as a key — superseded by the same path. |
| `scan_keys_all.py` | `harvest_keys.py` with a better target set; superseded the same way. |
| `try_keys.py` | Tests captured keys against real ciphertext — that test is `keyscan::recover`. |
| `ev2_grab.py` | The entire Python pipeline, harvest through merge; the Rust `grab` does all of it, including resume. |
| `drive_playhead.py` | Posts arrow keys to steer the playhead; `evmedia-win::playhead` does this, and its docstring says so. |

### Cannot work against this build — deleted

| Script | Why it goes |
| --- | --- |
| `ev2_batch.py` | Derives keys from manifests with the documented salt formula. That formula does not hold in this build, so without a salt it has no route to a key. |
| `hunt_salt.py` | Searches for the `tk + filename + salt` concatenation in memory. The decisive negative is that this build never builds that string. |
| `compare_tk.py` | Exists only to feed the tk-derivation family, which is the same disproven formula. |
| `find_b64.py` | Locates the base64 decoder by watching alphabet tables; repeated full-memory runs found nothing, and ticket 06 no longer needs the decoder. |
| `aes_map.py` | Static function-boundary mapping of the AES region. **Deleted on a false premise — see the correction below.** |
| `aes_disasm.py` | Same static route to the same RVA. **Deleted on a false premise — see the correction below.** |
| `disas.py` | Same static route again, against a live module; it times out. |
| `walk_aes.py` | Hooks the AES T-table site and walks up to its caller. The callers live in heap-generated code, so the walk reaches nothing — that is the finding, not a bug in the script. |
| `hexdiff.py` | The differential scan is broken (returns in 0.1 s with zero rows, i.e. it never scanned), and its question is now asked directly by ticket 07's write breakpoint, which needs no diff. |
| `_extract.py` | A one-off that pulled text out of a single, long-superseded session transcript into a log. It is not apparatus for anything pending. |
| `find_segments.ps1` | Its RVAs point at this build's M3U8 parser, not at key derivation. It has failed every time it was run. |

### Correction: two of those deletions rested on a premise that is false

`aes_map.py` and `aes_disasm.py` were deleted here as "cannot work against this build", because the
note this project was carrying said static analysis was unavailable: *"静态分析不可用：无
capstone/pefile/dumpbin"*. **That is wrong.** Both `capstone` (5.0.7) and `pefile` (2024.8.26) are
installed in `C:\Users\Yonjay\.conda\envs\subgen`, and `PlayerLibRender56_vs.dll` is **not packed** —
six normal sections and a `.pdata` table with 19,488 function entries. The whole DLL is statically
analysable from the file, and was, in the course of preparing ticket 06: the app's AES key setup
(`0x20EC0`), its block-call trampoline (`0x20EA0`) and the two consumers of the segment-key field were
all located that way without a player.

The likely origin of the false note is the interpreter. The PATH `python` on this machine is the
Microsoft Store placeholder and has neither package; the conda one has both. A note written after
running the wrong `python` reads exactly like an absence of the tool.

The second half of the original reasoning was wrong too: it said the entry points those scripts sought
were "already known", but `0x792c78` is an instruction in the middle of a function, not an entry, and
the correct way to get the entry is `.pdata` — not the `cc cc cc` scan this ticket's sibling suggested.

Both files are recoverable from git (`git show de68f47:tools/parser-tools/aes_map.py`). They were not
restored, because what they did is now done better and directly by `.pdata` plus capstone. But the
verdict recorded against them here was wrong, and the reason above is the record of how.

### Wrappers on the dead offline path — deleted

- `一键抓取.cmd` — exists only to run `find_segments.ps1`.
- `解密转MP4.cmd` — consumes the `evplayer2_manifest.json` that `find_segments.ps1` would have produced, so it cannot run either.

The vendored third-party directories and the two `.zip` archives (`EVPlayer2_解密工具与参数/`,
`EVPlayer2通用解密工具/`, and both zips) are **left in place**. They are not bench scripts, they are
tracked, and the zips are the authoritative copy of the vendor material. They sit on the same dead
offline path as the two wrappers above — worth knowing, but removing someone else's artefact is not
this ticket.

### Instruments — kept untouched

These are what tickets 06–10 draw from. `probe_urls.py` and `capture_all.py` overlap (the latter is
the v6 successor to the former); both are kept, because pruning apparatus mid-experiment is the thing
this ticket exists to avoid.

- **Ticket 06 (the API AES as an oracle):** `probe_at.py`, `hook_aes_key.py`, `find_aes_key.py`, `extract_bodies.py`.
- **Ticket 07 (the instruction that writes a segment key):** `probe_at.py`, `probe_schedule_key.py`, `wait_ready.py`, and `watch_key.py` — the last of which cannot be run as it stands. **Added after this classification, not part of the thirteen:** `tools/parser-tools/probe_write.py`, written when ticket 07 was made ready to run. `watch_key.py` is the only survivor that can arm a memory write watch and it is the one that hangs the player, so waiting on it would have cost the session the ticket exists for. Ticket 07 records what replaced it and why.
- **Ticket 08 (the `getDownEVSKey` plaintext):** `capture_all.py`, `sniff_plain.py`, `fish_api_plain.py`, `probe_urls.py`.
- **Both / general:** `hook_caller.py`, `find_in_mem.py`.

The count is therefore fourteen Python scripts on the bench today, not the thirteen this ticket left. The fourteenth arrived with ticket 07's preparation, after the classification was made.

### Dependency check

Nothing the product or the remaining experiments need was deleted. A repo-wide search for each
deleted name found only: `HANDOFF.md` (historical narrative, handled in ticket 05), `captured/harvest_all.log`
(capture evidence, which stays), and `scan_keys_all.py` inside the harvest family, deleted with it.
`disas.py`'s only other match is `tools/device_analysis/disasm.py`, a different file in a different
directory, untouched.

test: bring the storm harness into the repo, and correct what it was measured to say

storm_test.py drives a stand-in target (storm.rs) that did not exist when the bench's
earlier measurements were taken, and the reason it exists is that those
measurements were made on stand-ins too small to falsify them: one page, one
thread, sleeping between stores. This one has 24 pages read in tight loops by four
threads, then 24 stores at page+0x120. It extracts the JavaScript out of
probe_write.py rather than copying it, so it cannot drift from the thing it
measures.

Its results were first recorded with more confidence than the sampling supports.
Repeat runs show 24, 8 and 4 guarded pages failing every time, 2 pages returning
the full result in four runs of five, and 1 page in every run -- while one
unthrottled run at 1 page passed and one throttled run at 2 pages failed. So the
direction is solid (more pages is worse, the rate limit helps) and the boundary is
not. MAX_PAGES is 2 because 4 never worked and 1 always did, not because 2 was
shown to be the exact edge, and both the docstring and ticket 07 now say so
outright instead of quoting a number nobody repeated.

interval_test.py is kept for the same honesty: it is the control that proved
setInterval works in this frida build, which is how a harness bug that made the
heartbeat look starved was caught rather than written up as a defect.

Ticket 03 records the addition under its existing "added after this
classification" precedent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

`tools/parser-tools/storm/`:

- [storm_test.py](tools/parser-tools/storm/storm_test.py) — 驱动器。**它从 `probe_write.py` 里抽取 JS 原文来跑,不是复制一份**,所以不可能和目标漂移。
- [interval_test.py](tools/parser-tools/storm/interval_test.py) — 对照实验,单独验证 `setInterval` 在这个 frida 构建里能周期触发。留着它是因为正是它把一个脚手架 bug 和「仪器坏了」区分开了。

路径全部用 `__file__` 解析,我在仓库里实跑了两遍确认能用——放进去跑不起来等于没放。

## 我先前那张表太干净了,已改正

第一次记录时我把结果写成了一张整齐的、每格一个数的表,并据此断言「2 页是上限、限速是关键」。搬进来后重采样:

| 守护页数 | 次数 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 24 / 8 / 4 | 各 1 | 每次都失败 |
| 2 | 5 | 4 次成功,**1 次失败** |
| 1 | 3 | 每次成功 |
| 2、去掉限速 | 2 | 每次都失败 |
| 1、去掉限速 | 1 | **成功** |

**方向是稳的**(页数越多越糟、限速有用),**边界是不稳的**。所以 `MAX_PAGES = 2` 的理由改成了「4 从来没成功过、1 每次都成功」,而不是「2 被证明正好是边界」;`probe_write.py` 的 docstring 和工单 07 都写明:不要引用比这更紧的数字,除非你重复验证过。
